object_description: angular sports center formed by two buildings beneath a connected roof
design_condition: The two buildings are set laterally to preserve the spacious outdoor landscape and frame the pool area, but the large roof and extensive footprint intrude into the park and conflict with its free-flowing topography.

positive.statement: The lateral setting brings back a significant increase in space and the original spaciousness of the outdoor area.

position.rationale: Open landscape is located around the separated building masses, especially toward the southern and eastern site edges.

positive.statement: The central hall creates a clear and easily found entrance gate to the facility.

position.rationale: The connecting junction between the two elongated masses provides the most plausible shared entrance location.

positive.statement: The architecture respects the necessary distance from the outdoor pool, allowing the landscape to flow around it.

position.rationale: The pool is not distinctly sampled; the open southern zone adjacent to the main building is used.

positive.statement: The operational arrangement of the ice rink promises good use.

position.rationale: The larger elongated building is the most plausible ice-rink volume, supported by its broad footprint and elevations.

positive.statement: The indoor pool is organized on one floor with a pleasant reference to the outdoor pool.

position.rationale: The indoor pool is not separately identifiable; it is approximated within the main hall volume.

positive.statement: The noise insulation of the open ice rink works well.

position.rationale: The open rink is not distinctly visible, so a low-level position beside the main volume is assigned.

positive.statement: The ideas for the wider area provide beneficial additions to the sports and leisure facility.

position.rationale: The comment concerns additions around the facility; the surrounding open southern site is the useful anchor.

negative.statement: The paths and terrain adjustments do not yet fit well into the existing park.
